verdict.rationale: Merchants get a documented self-serve start: a sandbox sign-up form with terms acceptance that enables test transactions, plus a public Trusted Agent Protocol spec. That spec includes getting-started snippets, Visa's public JWKS keys and a runnable merchant-side reference implementation, so a site can verify and admit legitimate agents on its own. Going live is not self-serve, though: production fees require contacting Visa, and the product is flagged as still in development and deployment. missing for 10: a self-serve production enablement path (setting toggle or click-through agreement), a documented end-to-end go-live checklist for merchants, independent or hands-on corroboration of merchant onboarding.
